title: Antoine de Bordeaux (London) to Brienne, 30 May 1653 NS, BL Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90 (Thurloe intercept)

documents.shelfmark: BL Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90 (DECODE R8390; duplicates R8391, R8393)

plaintext.source: No decipherment of the letter exists. The English Deciphering Branch's key sheet for 'Mr. Bordeaux' 1653 (BL Add MS 32263 f. 1, DECODE R7537) is a key, not a plaintext; it was the source of the reading.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's provisional transcription (810 tokens, 156 symbols), corrected against DECODE page images
transcription.notes: The provisional transcription merged two glyphs and dropped diacritics; that alone defeated the ciphertext-only solver.

system.summary: Letters as graphic signs and plain numbers 15-37; three diacritic-marked number series (prime, two dots, overbar) are alphabetical CV syllabaries with common words embedded; a few name codes.

diacritics.note: Prime, two dots and overbar on numbers select the syllable series; the clerk often omits them.

system.doubled_letters: ll is a sign of its own
system.sibling_key: Brienne's Cipher 2 (1651) and Lasry's key for Mazarin to Bordeaux (1654): same design, different values. Used for the design hypothesis only.
system.notes: 14 unread: name codes 25‾ 28‾ 43‾ 332 344 396‾ and the rare tokens 6¨ 10 30' 35' 68' 98 14' 46¨.

prior_solution.where: English Deciphering Branch key sheet, BL Add MS 32263 f. 1 (DECODE R7537)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the key sheet and page images.
tools: simulated annealing with monotone syllabary alignment (solver.py)

solution.what: Symbol classes, token counts and IC (0.019) on the provisional transcription.
Design A from sibling keys of the same office: marked series are alphabetical syllabaries, overbar and three-digit groups are nomenclature.
Plaintext sought in Birch (Thurloe SP i) and Guizot's despatches; 30 May 1653 in neither. Found DECODE R7537, the English key for 'Mr. Bordeaux' 1653.
Solver recovers 99 % on design-A controls of equal length; 52 % and 9 % when 10 % of diacritics are misread.
Ciphertext-only annealing on the real text, 21+ seeds over series orders and unit lists.
Transcribed key sheet R7537; it confirms design A exactly.
Checked the page images: 21 corrections, two merged glyphs split, lost marks restored.
Applied the key plus context-derived additions; letter read except name codes and rare tokens.
Duplicate of the ending (R8391) agrees token for token; content fits the Ormée negotiations of May 1653.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Item A (R8390, BL Add MS 4200 f. 88) was read with the English Deciphering Branch key sheet DECODE R7537 (BL Add MS 32263 f. 1, a separate key volume), found during the attempt after a ciphertext-only solver failed, then extended from context and checked against the page images and the duplicates R8391/R8393.
outcome.notes: Solver failure explained by transcription noise, as the noisy control predicted.
